body:
Strata's SYCL queues, uploads and recorded graphs could retain pointers after their backing storage was reused or released. This draft fixes the reviewed ownership and completion boundaries and integrates upstream tag v0.1.40.2 (`e8ca9afd03d839d4f8dbbe82dffce7f8a3bafd7a`). The unmodified upstream has a reproducible 32K baseline. Original integrated-fork timings remain rejected because its states/outputs differ. A later private DD5 candidate now passes repeated full-state/head 32K controls, clean 32K comparisons and the complete physical 262,144-cell lifecycle sequence. A separate one-object QSA reduction passes four fresh 32K numerical reads/disk continuation and sixteen quiet matched 32K comparisons: later PP improves 1.345%, while pooled TG is slower. It now also passes its own complete physical 256K lifecycle, including every saved state/KV tensor byte against DD5 and actual disk restoration. The timing sample does not establish a decode benefit; no production adoption follows. Production and accepted binaries remain unchanged; this PR remains a draft.

Changes:

- Own and drain queues before storage destruction; keep borrowed queues alive, finish staging/MTP uploads before reuse, propagate asynchronous errors and validate USM/VMM properties. Retire graphs before releasing backing weights and restore from immutable RAM weights before publishing readiness.
- Preserve explicit per-layer cache count and residency. Check each backed slot span before pointer formation or copying. Fix the merge reconciliation that combined incompatible profile-order slot sizes and per-layer admission.
- Use defined byte/word and float-array access while retaining ordered FMAs, including upstream's MoE combine4. Remove independent-launch flags from 53 reviewed kernels; retain flags where persistent/global coordination requires them. Fail closed on the allocation alias check's final retry/null result; sparse sampling does not prove every byte.
- Reject unvalidated shared queue forks, fused one-token GDN history commit and batched pipeline modes before GPU work. Experimental weight release and expert queue pacing remain off by default.
- Keep bounded GDB/PTY observation with process identity checks, owned cleanup and main-thread snapshots. First correctness checks record flushed UR/Level Zero calls and parameter validation; speed measurements omit diagnostics and require at least 32,768 input tokens.

Validation on Arc B570 10 GiB, Ryzen 5 5600X, 128 GiB RAM; kernel 7.0.0-38, NEO 26.31.39395.14, oneAPI 2026.1.1, Level Zero V2; direct submission, persistent cache and copy offload disabled:

- Production build, 562 server tests (8 skips), 30 setup scripts, 5 standalone CPU tests, 168 bitwise CPU-pool cases, Q8_K byte parity, 8 queue/lifetime suites and ASan/UBSan cache-copy bounds checks passed.
- Three short normal-MTP controls complete first/repeat/other/restored requests; all 12 match historical IDs, logprobs and all 248,320 first-head floats. Short timings are functional preflight only and excluded from speed comparisons.
- Upstream runs in an independent clean clone/worktree without local patches. The matched 32,768-token fixture uses 8192-token chunks, int8 KV and normal MTP4. Two clean upstream repetitions average **393.65 PP / 17.14 TG tok/s**, with identical IDs/logprobs in both repetitions and the logged control. Its SYCL version string remains 0.1.40-sycl; source and binary hashes identify the release.
- Both original fork repetitions complete with 64 finite-logprob outputs, normal exit, owned cleanup and no new xe fault. Their observed average is 334.93 / 16.96 tok/s, **rejected as a tuning reference** because repetition 1 diverges at output index 34. Actual cache allocations differ between arms: upstream 144 slots / 281 MiB, fork 128 / 325 MiB. That difference does not explain variation within the same fork configuration.
- Capturing state before decode localizes one differing fork pair to GDN state at model layer 14 and QSA state at layer 15; its earliest differing QSA row is token 8200, in the second 8K chunk. Earlier GDN/QSA state is byte-identical. This establishes a prefill discrepancy, without identifying the producing operation or proving undefined behavior.
- `MKL_CBWR=AUTO` gives two matching full state/head/output captures, then differs in the third fresh 32K run. It is not a reproduction fix. Disabling implicit counter-event conversion also does not establish reproducibility or eliminate all counter/profiling waits. Neither setting is adopted globally.
- A private actual-DMA completion candidate passes CPU lifetime/ring tests, ASan/UBSan and one logged 32K comparison of all 66 prefill state parts, the full head and output. Its next run stops in native counter-event status/timestamp processing and is rejected. No experimental completion or copy-queue candidate is part of the production source.
- Omitting copy-queue profiling gives three matching fresh 32K state/head/output captures. The directly owned prototype remains rejected because it bypasses the global-wait registry. A registered factory preserves that contract, rebuilds every translation unit with the same header, and matches production Strata/GGML/compiler settings. Three full state/head controls with CNR and another three without CNR match their respective production controls, with normal exit, owned cleanup and no new xe fault. The production source has no experimental completion or copy-queue change.
- A scheduling-only private candidate removes 14 prefill root-sync properties while retaining kernel bodies, arithmetic, ranges, subgroups, queues and drains. Three exact full state/head 32K checks pass. Four subsequent dump-free 32K timing jobs use registered/no-root/no-root/registered (ABBA), each generating 64 normal-MTP tokens; every ID/logprob matches its captured control. Registered copy averages **406.78 PP / 16.96 TG tok/s**; no-root averages **408.52 / 16.06**. The prompt difference is below the control's repeat spread, and decode varies within an arm; two repetitions do not establish a useful speed change. These are private-candidate measurements with implicit conversion forced off and no CNR, separate from the earlier upstream comparison.
- Removing only the implicit-counter-conversion override on the same scheduling binary also passes three fresh 32K comparisons of all 66 state parts, all 248,320 head floats, all 64 IDs and every logprob. Both that override and MKL CNR are absent; other common process settings remain explicit. These state-dump/diagnostic durations are excluded from throughput. All 13 new no-CNR/scheduling/clean/default-counter jobs exit normally with complete owned cleanup and no new xe fault. Neither candidate is adopted, and these checks do not prove general hang prevention or full-context safety.


- Host-only Intel PTI unitrace profiling on the unchanged private scheduling executable passes a logged32K check, quiet32K profile and unprofiled32K control, matching all66state parts,248,320head floats,64IDs and all logprobs. The actual collector options leave device/kernel tracing and metrics off; actual target environment and executable identity are captured. About2.23million native status queries across three worker threads and503,650 kernel appends occur in the request envelope. Concurrent API intervals do not measure CPU utilization, GPU busy time or PCIe DMA. Boot/raw clock alignment is approximate and sensitivity is recorded; captured/profiled durations are excluded from throughput claims.
- A separate environment-only attention128/layout1 experiment retains subgroup32, kernel source, queues and ordered arithmetic. Three fresh32K full-state/head/output controls pass before a clean default/128-layout1/128-layout1/default ABBA comparison. Two runs per setting average **408.30 PP /16.35 TG tok/s** for default32/layout0 and **408.36 /16.72** for128/layout1. The **+0.014% prompt difference** does not establish a useful gain. Decode varies within the default arm; this prefill setting does not establish its cause. All ten new host-profile/attention/state/clean jobs exit normally with exact controls, complete owned cleanup and no new xe fault. No candidate is adopted; full262,144-cell serving and PP1000/TG70 remain open.

- Processing-order controls on the same private executable first check compact storage/layout 1, then layer-major RAM residuals, then all-GPU residuals with MTP decode-only release and immutable-RAM restoration. Nine fresh 32K captures match all 66 main-prefill state parts, all 248,320 first-head floats, 64 IDs and every logprob. The GPU condition also verifies every released MTP expert/head payload byte before/after restoration. Six subsequent clean 32K jobs run default/RAM/GPU/GPU/RAM/default. Two-run means are **408.28 PP / 17.10 TG**, **338.11 / 16.96** and **422.59 / 17.32 tok/s**. GPU prefill averages +3.5%, but its pair differs by about 11%; this does not establish a reproducible improvement. RAM residuals measure 17.2% below default. Main cache weights remain backed in all arms.
- Clean GPU-row runs unmap **939,524,096 physical MTP bytes in about 22.5 ms** and restore **931,016,700 RAM payload bytes in 247.955 / 248.489 ms**, including mapping and copying. Graphs are retired before unmapping and recaptured when needed; payload verification is off during timing. All 15 new requests retain exact outputs and the control's 43 accepted / 66 offered MTP counts, exit normally, complete owned cleanup and record no new xe fault. These counts do not compare every internal MTP tensor. Fixed 32,767-row GPU storage is not validated at full context; the previous second-prefill memory failure remains open. The matched main-cache partial/full/snapshot follow-up is reported below. This private candidate is not adopted.

- Main-cache lease follow-up uses the same private binary and a matched 64 MiB segmented allocation in every arm. Kept backing, half release/RAM, full release/RAM and full release/snapshot each pass a first logged 32K request and two fresh complete main-state/head/output captures. All twelve match 66 state parts, all 248,320 head floats, 64 IDs/logprobs and 43/66 MTP counts. Half release unmaps **201,326,592 physical bytes**, verifying all **130,731,008 occupied tail bytes** before/after restoration; full release unmaps **402,653,184 bytes** and verifies all **281,651,200 occupied RAM-source bytes** (snapshot checks the full logical tail). Same virtual addresses and slots are retained; queues drain and graphs retire before unmap, with recapture after restoration. Captured times are excluded. These fresh serve processes do not warm verifier graphs at startup: released arms capture all legal sizes at restoration, while kept backing captures on first use. Thus the callback includes initial capture/kernel loading, and the clean means include different capture schedules; the later full-RAM32K captured repeat gate passes, while matched quiet repeated performance and full-context capacity still need separate gates.
- Eight fresh clean 32K jobs run kept/half-RAM/full-RAM/full-snapshot and reverse, without diagnostics, validation, payload checks, dumps, profiler, transfer timing or extra waits. Two-run means are **443.28 PP / 16.89 TG**, **443.76 / 17.70**, **433.31 / 17.36** and **442.24 / 17.83 tok/s**. Half release is only +0.11% prompt throughput; full RAM is -2.25%, snapshot -0.23%. This fixed-8192-chunk comparison establishes no useful prefill gain from release alone. Decode varies within an arm and is not attributed to a prefill-only setting. All twenty captured/clean jobs match output and MTP counts, exit normally, complete owned cleanup and record no new xe fault.
- Full-RAM restore excluding its graph callback takes **51.588 / 52.091 ms**, including remap/copy/zero-fill/wait. Graph callback intervals range **537.714–1004.037 ms** among released arms. Snapshot suspension takes **220.314 / 221.539 ms**, and restore excluding graphs **61.198 / 60.502 ms**. These are measured phase intervals, not full-VRAM PCIe bandwidth. Increasing chunk/residual capacity using freed memory remains a separate pending comparison; no private candidate is adopted.
- Actual cache-lease code passes 19 CPU ASan/UBSan cases for mid-expert release, current/adaptive residency, validation failures, partial-shrink rollback and grow/refresh retries. The same cases pass with byte-varying payloads; a pinned mutant omitting the intra-expert RAM offset is rejected by the actual pre-unmap comparison. This CPU proof does not establish SYCL mapping, all runtime UB absent or full-context safety. The 262,144-cell occupancy/repeat/restore/clipped-tail/refusal/later-valid gates remain mandatory, and no private candidate is adopted.

Remaining limitations:

Full 262,144-cell normal-MTP serving, repeat/restore, clipped tail, refusal and a later valid request have not all passed on this release. Long-prefill waits remain unresolved. One further production 32K check has a xe CCS engine reset; other stopped checks have no new xe fault. Their processes are cleaned up, and subsequent logged H2D/kernel/D2H health checks pass on the same boot without reset/rebind/reboot. Stack traces identify the observed native waits; they do not prove a driver root cause or prevention. Additional `STRATA_PREFILL_SYNC=1` phase waits also stop a short diagnostic and are excluded. The intermediate merge's CPU copy overrun was a local reconciliation bug, now fixed and bounds-tested. The earliest overwritten compiler log is explicitly documented.

- A larger-chunk control keeps input at **32,768 tokens** and grows compact chunks to **12,288** on the unchanged private executable. Actual extracted accounting matches the executed 8K layout; the 12K workspace is 2,738,729,216 B, new GPU residuals 838,819,840 B, and the engine budget estimates a net 708,837,376 B increment. The logged/validated request fits and exits normally without a new xe fault, but **fails the mathematical gate**: 63/66 state parts and all 248,320 head floats differ (max absolute 0.873567, RMS 0.180161); the third generated ID changes, and MTP counts are 38/75 rather than 43/66. No quiet speed comparison or adoption follows. Chunk/GEMM/callback boundaries have not been isolated as the cause; the subsequent exact-word GPU health check passes.
- The saved 12K native logs show reported free VRAM decreasing by **921.152 MiB** from prefill entry to restored weights. Main restore plus initial verifier capture grows physical backing by 384 MiB and requests only 1,114,112 B of device USM, while reported free falls by 1,221.324 MiB; 680 command lists and 61 modules are created in that interval. All logged device USM and native modules/kernels/command lists are destroyed at exit. This is allocation/resource evidence, not proof of a leak, a clean timing result, or a solution to the older full-context repeat failure. Full 262,144-cell occupancy/repeat/restore/clipped-tail/refusal/later-valid gates remain open.

[Main-cache actual-code CPU checks and completed 32K lease controls](https://github.com/yqYo1/Strata/blob/sync/upstream-2026-10-05/bench/results/2026-10-05-sycl-prefill-scaling/upstream-v0.1.40.2-20261008/code32k/repro32k/main-cache-release-and-restore/README.md)

[Rejected larger compact chunk, accounting and first-capture/native-resource audit](https://github.com/yqYo1/Strata/blob/sync/upstream-2026-10-05/bench/results/2026-10-05-sycl-prefill-scaling/upstream-v0.1.40.2-20261008/code32k/repro32k/larger-compact-chunk-12k/README.md)


### Same-process 32K graph and state validation

- Three fresh processes each reread the complete 32,768-token input three times, with reuse disabled. All nine raw66-part states, complete first heads,64 IDs/logprobs and MTP43/66 match the hard control. Each dump is newly written and preserved. All processes exit normally without forced cleanup, survivors or new xe faults; captured/validated durations are excluded from speed comparisons.
- Successful UR traces release680 main command buffers and6 MTP buffers before later physical unmaps, then create/finalize680 main buffers after restoration. Native command lists remain704 during reuse, while all UR references and tracked native resources reach zero at exit. Source checks separately cover queue drain and stable-address/payload restoration.
- API-log-free capture processes reproduce the reported-free decline: prefill entry2153.496 →1131.254 →1120.297 MiB. Later main warm adds no native module/kernel/list/device-USM objects, yet384 MiB remapping accompanies394.707/389.449 MiB reported-free reductions. This does not isolate resident heaps, prove a leak or establish steady state.
- Only the captured full-RAM32K already-used-graph repeat gate is closed. Matched quiet repeats and full262,144-cell occupancy/repeat/restore/clipped-tail/refusal/later-valid remain open. Every performance comparison uses at least32,768 input tokens, with initial loading/capture separated from later full rereads. Production binaries/defaults are unchanged; PP1000/TG70 remains active.


The offline runtime-cache follow-up retains official UR source at`95ed2199` with explicit uncertainty about its match to the installed adapter. Regular command-list release returns native lists to a per-context cache; an installed env string does not establish that an event-cache switch affects this path. The standard EventPool-only log count is zero, while an intermediate event-handle parser lacks counter-event extension coverage; no complete event balance or Linux VRAM remedy is inferred from the Windows A770 host-memory issue. Both older full-context attempts already enabled main and MTP release, so this release alone cannot be claimed to resolve their failures. No new runtime or cache switch is adopted; reducing native graph/list footprint remains a separately gated implementation candidate.


### Private KV-streaming candidate, compiled only

Existing`--kv-resident 32768` is an avenue to reduce full-context resident KV; earlier accepted32K jobs use mode0 and do not validate it. Before activation, an isolated source candidate replaces competing same-slot hit stamp/reference writes with relaxed device-scope atomic stores, reads packed host counters with`memcpy`, and removes four unused reset/resolve/copy/ring root-sync properties while preserving SG32/WG1024 and arithmetic. Sorted selections`[16,32]`/`[4,16]` demonstrate different query lanes hitting page4. This is a dormant-path source issue, not a claim it caused prior non-streaming hangs.

The candidate compiles/links with accepted e82 flags and changes only the KV object in a copied kernel archive. Every other member/link input and baseline/production binary remains unchanged. Executable SHA256:`4af18d831559e68215090d55ddba878986a07af61d834485351af81d793d6e77`. It is **not GPU-tested or adopted**. Host-USM ownership/cleanup, ring/staging/clipping and snapshot reconstruction are pending source gates, followed by logged32K state/head/output/count checks, matched quiet inputs≥32K and the complete262,144-cell gates. The preparer's wrong expected root-property count is caught before source output; both immutable CPU versions and build logs are retained.


### RAM-authoritative KV and matched repeated 32K processing order

The earlier v2 KV binary remains unrun. Its v3 successor `1441ad556cb1d8ecddf42e525a1462cc53f9251fae4734c008046e10e8b0e599` additionally pairs the page-table claim with an atomic read, replaces device counter/vector representation aliases with memcpy, and checks host-USM/WG1024/SG32 support. It inherits shared-hit atomics, defined host counter reads and four unused root-property removals. These mode1 accesses are not attributed as causes of older mode0 hangs.

A private prefill candidate `79e8a19b0ba8cb06b9d632f4528a134204c0fa15f6522fa0c75c523c730ca35b` permits mode1 in existing single-device layer-major processing, requiring owned identity staging and no KV prefetch. Existing in-order stage/append/attention stays unchanged. It uses RAM residuals and full main/MTP RAM leases; no prefix-retention optimization is added.

Both configurations complete three full32768-token/64-output requests in one logged/validated process at context262144/resident32768. All66 used main-state parts, every248320 first-head float,64IDs/logprobs and MTP43/66 match the hard control. First raw state matches too; later differences only involve unwritten rounded-page future cells. Both exit0 without forced cleanup, survivors or new xe faults. The first source-authority guard rejected a worktree-versus-pinned-prefill mismatch before GPU use; its negative and corrected review are retained.

Quiet ABBA uses four fresh processes, three complete32768 reads each, with common8192/int8/cache128/workers5/pcie0/MTP4 settings and resume0. API traces, state/head/payload checks, profiler/TRACE and extra phase waits are absent. Initial request after READY and later full rereads are separated:
- Chunk-major: first393.43 PP/16.54 TG; repeated427.49 PP/18.48 TG.
- Layer-major with RAM residual/main+MTP leases: first324.63 PP/17.94 TG; repeated429.45 PP/17.92 TG.

Repeated prefill improves0.46%, while decode declines3.03%; this configuration has no substantial speed gain in these readings. All18 model requests retain exact64IDs/logprobs/counts, and six owned GDB/inferior jobs exit cleanly. [Source, receipts and individual results](https://github.com/yqYo1/Strata/blob/ebac0156711ff8176a6cc202a2a1a2d264bd5731/bench/results/2026-10-05-sycl-prefill-scaling/upstream-v0.1.40.2-20261008/code32k/repro32k/kv-streaming-32k-and-layer-order-v3/README.md) are archived; all2884 manifest entries are hashed and tracked, with huge logs/state images/binaries private by hash.

Production c88f94d, accepted e82fc5 and main remain unchanged. Context256K as a configured limit does not prove full262144 occupancy: last physical cell262143, repeated full prefill, restored state, clipped tails/refusals and later valid>=32K remain mandatory before adoption. PP1000/TG70 remains active and unachieved; no merge or global/runtime/recovery change occurs.


### Visible commits and the full-capacity indexer spare

A 32768-token input capped at 64 outputs saved 32833 consumed tokens instead of 32831. A private candidate clips the accepted prefix at max_new/EOS before commit in serial/pipeline serve and CLI speculation, preserving verifier window sizes and numerical rows. Twelve CPU ASan/UBSan cases pass. The initial logged 32K gate preserves the complete head, used prefill state and all 64 IDs/logprobs. SAVE contains exactly prompt plus outputs except the last; visible MTP counts become 41/66 after excluding invisible commits.

Two fresh 262140-input/4-output reads, separated by a different fresh 32K input, reach physical cell262143 with RESUME0 and match heads, used state, output IDs/logprobs and MTP counts. Both saved images contain all13 main/MTP KV layers through262144 cells. Every saved state/KV byte matches, with no tensor exclusions. Actual 32K disk restoration reproduces the reference continuation.

The full disk roundtrip is rejected: only each main layer's last512-byte pooled row65535 changes. The restored row equals live idx_dead; the saved row does not. Speculative computation can complete a block that partial commit does not retain, leaving that block key in the live spare. The process receives QUIT and exits0 normally without forced cleanup, survivors or new kernel faults; restored clipped-tail/refusal/later32K tests are not reached.

A separately compiled kernel candidate restores the spare after replaying the accepted positions, including trailing -1 positions. Arithmetic, local memory, existing barriers, subgroup32, launch geometry, queues and other kernel/archive members remain unchanged. Its initial fresh32K head/used-state/64IDs/logprobs/MTP gate passes, SAVE has the exact32831 consumed visible-prefix IDs, and all12 main spares equal idx_dead. The same owned r5 process completes its first full read with reference head/used-state/IDs/logprobs parity, reaches cell262143, and saves all13 full images with each main spare equal to idx_dead. Its interposed fresh32K control also matches. The second full read subsequently stops in the host watchdog at layer33/chunk196608 after60s without progress, with SIGABRT on watchdog thread82. No new kernel fault is recorded; all owned processes are gone and post-exit device/runtime health passes. Repeated-full, actual disk-roundtrip, restored clipped-tail/refusal/later32K were not completed, so this is not a full-capacity/adoption pass. [Terminal negative, exact byte diagnosis, private source/build receipts and the initial32K snapshot](https://github.com/yqYo1/Strata/blob/806eab62/bench/results/2026-10-05-sycl-prefill-scaling/upstream-v0.1.40.2-20261008/code32k/repro32k/indexer-spare-full256k-rejection-and-candidate-v1/README.md) are archived.

A separate prefill host-polling candidate uses32 initial yields followed by requested10us sleeps. CPU sanitizer/cancellation/deadline checks and actual shadow-header selection pass; it is not GPU-tested or combined with the indexer candidate. Synthetic query counts are not CPU utilization, transfer or inference measurements. The public host-wait comment now acknowledges that a runtime status query can block beyond the host budget. [Partial first-image and polling evidence](https://github.com/yqYo1/Strata/blob/806eab62/bench/results/2026-10-05-sycl-prefill-scaling/upstream-v0.1.40.2-20261008/code32k/repro32k/visible-output-commit-full-first-and-poll-backoff-v2/README.md) retains its original capture scope.

All speed comparisons use inputs of at least32768 tokens, with initial and repeated full reads separated. Logged correctness durations are excluded. Production/accepted binaries, main and the unpatched upstream baseline remain unchanged; no reset/rebind/reboot/service/package/global action or merge occurs. PP1000/TG70 remains active and unachieved.

### Consistent DPCT definitions before profiler tuning

Actual preprocessing reveals different tokens for the same dpct/device.hpp class-inline queue factory and external-inline sync_barrier in translated versus hand-written TUs: source-local DPCT_PROFILING_ENABLED changes the profiling property and barrier versus single-task operation. This conflicts with the matching-definition requirement in the [C++ one-definition rule](https://eel.is/c++draft/basic.def.odr); it is not a demonstrated cause of prior hangs.

A private shadow header keeps the translated profiling branch uniformly. Actual preprocessed definitions match between both commands and the old translated branch, while the explicit nonprofiling copy factory remains unchanged. The original strata link has116 compile commands,67 actual device-header users and seven unprofiled users. Only these seven objects in three copied archives are recompiled/replaced on the7f054 indexer base; all other members/link inputs remain unchanged. The new dd5efb executable compiles/links, and its separate logged gate passes four fresh32768-token reads alternating two inputs, complete head/used-state/output/logprob/MTP comparisons, actual32K disk-restored continuation and normal owned exit. It remains unadopted pending the physical256K and quiet speed gates. Include-selection/parser negatives and the corrected -H/actual-dependency proof are retained.

A separate777449 polling executable rebases only the CPU-tested prefill object/archive onto7f054. It is GPU-untested and will need a proved compatible baseline for an isolated comparison. Installed VTune2026.4/build632893 CLI version/help confirms xpu-offload option names with CPU sampling/hardware metrics/stacks/bandwidth/power disabled and programming API tracing enabled. No collector is run; B570 support and actual device timestamp/graph coverage are unproven. [Intel's release notes](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/release-notes/vtune-profiler/current.html) document improved reused LevelZero/SYCL graph tracing, excluding native graphs.

[First repaired full-image snapshot, uniform-header receipts, polling rebase and help-only profiler preparation](https://github.com/yqYo1/Strata/blob/85d460f4/bench/results/2026-10-05-sycl-prefill-scaling/upstream-v0.1.40.2-20261008/code32k/repro32k/profile-definition-audit-and-poll-rebase-v1/README.md) are archived. The historical full-first snapshot precedes the r5 host-watchdog abort; the separate uniform-header32K numerical gate is now complete. All speed inputs remain>=32768, diagnostic durations are excluded, production/accepted/main stay unchanged and PP1000/TG70 remains active.

### Terminal watchdog evidence and completed uniform-header32K gate

The stopped main thread waits in Stager::wait for CPU host-buffer readiness while three staging workers query DMA counter events that stay SUBMITTED/NOT_READY.
